textual.observation: The source presents purchasing a $3,500 founder pool as producing a stated return of $6,212 over nine months.

evidence.quote: in this new account I have $3,500 for buying a founder pool and in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars

textual.context: Presented during a review of an investment account; the source does not independently establish whether the result is typical, verified, or endorsed beyond the speaker's presentation.
textual.potential_relevance: A specific monetary return is linked to purchasing a founder pool, making the investment promotion and its conditions relevant for later review.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish that the stated amount was actually received, that the account or pool exists, or that the return is representative.

textual.observation: The source describes continued Bitcoin interest and an investment lasting indefinitely, while also stating that the value may decline and rise.

evidence.quote: you will continue receiving interest in Bitcoins I'm sure Bitcoin will move forward
of course it'll possibly go down then grow again
And this investment will last for the eternity

textual.context: The statements are part of the speaker's investment commentary and include a qualification that the value may go down before rising.
textual.potential_relevance: A continuing return and indefinite-duration claim is associated with the investment, while the same source acknowledges possible price movement in both directions.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the contractual terms, duration, likelihood, or availability of the claimed interest.

there will be another level, the income there may show a hundred times or even 1000 times more money

textual.context: This is stated in a promotional investment discussion; the wording and the exact requirements for attracting partners are unclear in the ASR.
textual.potential_relevance: A recruitment-related step is connected to progression and a claim of substantially increased income, which makes the compensation and recruitment structure relevant for later review.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish what attracting partners requires, whether anyone was recruited, or whether the stated income comparison is achievable or typical.

visual.observation: A BitClub mining-pool interface displays multiple pools with shares, BTC earnings, paid amounts, unused amounts, and re-purchase totals. Nearby explanatory text states that earnings are credited to the account daily and that re-purchasing can acquire additional shares.
visual.context: The material is presented as a screen-recorded walkthrough of the BitClub mining-pool account interface; whether it is promotional, instructional, or evaluative is unclear from the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface links participation through shares and re-purchases with displayed BTC earnings and payouts, creating a return claim tied to an asset-related action.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish that the displayed balances, earnings, payments, or mining activity are genuine, completed, or available for withdrawal, and they do not show the full purchase terms.

visual.observation: A BitClub page states that a promotion gave 50 ClubCoin to new Founder Packages and separately says the giveaway had ended; the same notice mentions free CoinPay tokens being given away while the service continued.
visual.context: The visible notice explicitly presents the ClubCoin giveaway as ended, while describing a continuing or forthcoming CoinPay-token update.
visual.potential_relevance: The page links a stated digital-token reward to obtaining Founder Packages, with an explicit availability condition that the giveaway had ended.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show the package price, eligibility details, whether the CoinPay-token offer remained active, or whether any reward was delivered.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes purchasing BitClub founder pools as a passive-income mining investment, presenting a $3,500 purchase as producing $6,212 in nine months and suggesting continued long-term Bitcoin income. It also encourages participation through a team and level structure, with higher income associated with attracting partners, rather than merely reporting on or criticizing the offer.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S04 fits because the video links paid founder-pool purchases to recurring Bitcoin mining returns and presents the arrangement as passive income. S06 is separately supported by the visible level-up/team structure and the speaker's statement that attracting partners can lead to higher income.
